subject: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R

messages.author: d220f2cc7220f272
messages.subject: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R
parts:
Dear F. Matías.
Congratulations for your work. I am currently using the field ImageR library to count corn in tests with high resolution orthomosaic (8mm/pixels), but I am having problems due to the size (Gb) of the orthomosaic.
Could you suggest me some recommendations for orthomosaic of this type.
My computer has AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Eight-Core 3.20 GHz Processor, 64.0 GB RAM.

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R
parts:
Hi there,

Thanks for contacting us. Unfortunately R was not made for large and havier images as yours seem. But I believe you can evaluate some strategies as (1) increasing the R base memory following this link (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P20), (2) reducing resolution size (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P12), or even (3) working with single and individual images before making the large and heavier orthomosaic. In this last case, you can use the GPS location to identify from each plot the information or counting is coming from (I never did this before and I believe this strategy only works for Drones with RTK).

Let's see if someone here in the community has any other idea to help us.

Thanks,
Filipe
